knowledge_weighting.method: entry-weighted mean of O*NET 31.0 importance (Scale IM): entry targets weight 2; other linked occupations in Job Zone 4 or 5 (or the entry targets' Job Zone) weight 1; Manager, Chief, Postsecondary-faculty, All Other, Supervisor, Director and Treasurers and Controllers titles, and non-target occupations in other Job Zones, weight 0
knowledge_weighting.note: top_knowledge/top_skills are the unweighted mean over all linked occupations (kept for comparison); the outline uses the entry-weighted lists.

skipped_knowledge.reason: service and client-relations knowledge; the outline leaves it to internships, part-time work and the practice tasks rather than a course slot
management and planning knowledge matters most after several years of experience, so the outline gives it no course slot (a management elective is optional)
teaching and training others is built through presenting, tutoring and peer teaching in projects rather than a dedicated course

outline_elements.rule: English Language is placed in Year 1 general education; workplace and management elements (Customer and Personal Service, Administrative, Clerical, Administration and Management, Personnel and Human Resources, Education and Training) get no course slot unless the major's CIP series is about them; the next three elements go to Year 2 and up to three more (ordered by importance to the entry targets) to Year 3; if fewer than two remain for Year 3, knowledge rated at least 2.5 for the entry targets fills it

method.supervisory_tasks: task statement matches a supervisory/managerial pattern (supervise, provide supervision, direct and coordinate, direct the work/activities/staff of, manage staff/personnel/employees/workers/teams, oversee the work/staff, hire, subordinates, assign work to, evaluate the work/performance of, train and supervise); 'under supervision' does not count

quality_flags.note: Authored tier: entry targets and practice tasks were chosen and reviewed per major, so the generated-tier plausibility flags are not applied. Informational only: cited tasks whose O*NET statement is supervisory are listed; their authored scenarios say when they are practice for a later or graduate role.

entry_target_basis: Job Zone 4 linked occupations (excluding Manager/Chief/Postsecondary/All Other/Supervisor/Director/Treasurers and Controllers titles), ranked by similarity of their O*NET knowledge-importance profile to the average profile of the eligible linked occupations (Pearson correlation), base O*NET-SOC .00 codes first; then a documented DreamCo manual override (authored/target_overrides.json) changed the rule output (15-1243.00, 15-1252.00, 15-1255.00) to 15-1252.00, 15-1255.00, 15-1299.03

entry_target_review.reason: Database Architects was dropped as a mid-career architect role. Document Management Specialists (Job Zone 4) is added because records, metadata and content-management work is a core information-science destination. Software Developers and Web and Digital Interface Designers are kept.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A mid-sized city's planning department has 120,000 scanned and born-digital files (permits, site plans, council memos, public comments, inspection photos) sitting in shared drives with inconsistent folder names. Draft a classification taxonomy and metadata scheme for a new content-management system: top-level categories and two levels below, five to eight required metadata fields with controlled values, how retention and public-records status are captured, and how you would test the scheme with real staff searches.

rubric.description: Categories are mutually exclusive enough to file consistently and reflect how planning staff actually look things up (by parcel, project, document type).
Required fields use controlled vocabularies or formats (parcel ID pattern, dates), and public-records and retention status are captured.
Proposes testing with real tasks, such as staff filing samples or finding items, and measuring agreement or time to find.

reference_answer_outline: Top level by function (permits, plans, meetings, enforcement, public input), then project or parcel, then document type.
Required metadata: parcel ID, project number, document type, date, author unit, public-records flag, retention category.
Controlled lists for document type; validation pattern for parcel IDs.
Card-sort or tree-test with about ten staff; measure filing agreement and search success.
Plan for migrating legacy folders with automated suggestions plus manual review.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A regional food co-op tracks member volunteer hours in a spreadsheet shared by five coordinators; hours are lost, duplicate member records exist, and the board wants monthly reports. Gather what you would need to know and write a recommendation memo: current-state problems, three options (fix the spreadsheet with structure and validation, adopt an off-the-shelf volunteer tool, or build a small web app), a comparison on cost, effort, data quality and maintenance, your recommendation, and a rollout plan for the chosen option.

rubric.description: Problems are traced to causes (no unique member ID, free-text entry, concurrent editing) using evidence the student says they would collect.
Options are compared on consistent criteria including who maintains the solution after the student leaves.
The recommendation includes data cleanup, migration, training and a check that reports match after cutover.

reference_answer_outline: Interview coordinators and sample the sheet to count duplicates and gaps.
Option table: cost, setup time, data validation, reporting, maintenance burden, privacy.
Likely recommendation: an off-the-shelf tool or structured form plus database, since a custom build has no long-term maintainer.
Migration: deduplicate members on name plus email, import historical hours, reconcile totals.
Train coordinators; run the old and new systems in parallel for one month.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You designed the new course-catalog website for a community college: search with filters, course detail pages, and a 'plan my semester' view. Two front-end developers and one back-end developer start building next week. Write the collaboration plan: what you hand off (components, states, responsive breakpoints, accessibility notes), which decisions you need from the back-end developer (search API fields, response times), how design questions get answered during the build, and how you review the built pages against the design.

rubric.description: Handoff covers interaction states (empty, loading, error), responsive behavior and accessibility, not just static mockups.
Identifies what design needs from the back end (data fields, filter values, pagination) and flags design choices that affect performance.
Defines a regular review routine with acceptance criteria for design fidelity and accessibility.

reference_answer_outline: Component inventory with states and tokens (colors, spacing, type) in a shared design file.
Breakpoints for phone, tablet and desktop; keyboard and screen-reader notes for filters.
Questions for back end: which fields are searchable, filter counts, latency target, handling of sections with no seats.
Twice-weekly design check-ins and a shared question log with owners.
Review each page against acceptance criteria, including WCAG contrast and focus order.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A hospital's research office wants a document-management system for study protocols, consent-form versions, and regulatory correspondence; three research teams currently use email attachments and personal drives. Write a needs-assessment plan and a sample findings summary: who you will talk to, the questions you will ask, which existing documents you will inventory, how you will capture compliance needs (version control, audit trail, retention), and a prioritized list of requirements written as clearly invented example findings.

rubric.description: Includes coordinators, investigators, regulatory staff, IT and records management, not only managers.
Combines interviews, a document inventory, and observation of a real workflow such as a consent-form amendment.
Findings are written as testable requirements and ranked by risk and frequency; example findings are labeled as invented.

reference_answer_outline: Stakeholder list and a 30-minute interview guide on current workflow, pain points and must-not-lose items.
Inventory of document types, volume, and where the authoritative version lives.
Compliance needs: version history, approval trail, controlled access, retention schedule.
Requirements such as: only the current approved consent version can be downloaded for enrollment.
Ranked by risk (regulatory findings) and frequency of use.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A university wants a notification service that texts students when a seat opens in a full course section. Write a short design document: the components (enrollment feed, waitlist store, notifier, rate limiter), a simple queueing or load model that estimates peak messages per minute during registration week from stated assumptions, how that estimate drives design choices, and how you would measure in production whether the model was right.

rubric.description: Components and data flow are clear, including how duplicate or stale notifications are prevented.
The load estimate uses stated assumptions (students, sections, open-seat events per hour) and the arithmetic is shown and plausible.
Plans to compare predicted and observed load and adjust capacity or design if they diverge.

reference_answer_outline: Event-driven design: enrollment change triggers a check of the waitlist and queues notifications.
Assumptions such as 20,000 students and 3,000 full sections, with a peak of seat changes in the first hour; computes messages per minute.
Result drives queue size, SMS provider rate limit and batching.
Idempotency key per student and section to avoid duplicate texts; expiry if the seat is taken.
Dashboards on queue depth and send rate; compare with the model after the first registration day.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Your team redesigned the online form residents use to request a bulky-trash pickup from the city. Write two short documents: (1) a one-page help guide for residents, written at about an eighth-grade reading level and available in plain language for translation, and (2) a usability-test protocol for five participants that names the tasks, what you will observe, success criteria and how findings will be reported to the development team.

rubric.description: The help guide matches the form's steps, uses plain language and short sentences, and covers common errors.
Tasks are realistic, success criteria are observable, and the protocol includes consent and a think-aloud script.
Explains how findings are ranked by severity and turned into specific fixes for developers.

reference_answer_outline: Guide: what items qualify, step-by-step with screenshots placeholders, what happens after submitting, how to change a request.
Readability check with a standard formula; avoid idioms to ease translation.
Test tasks: request pickup for a couch, change the date, find out why a mattress is rejected.
Measures: task completion, time, errors, and post-task ease rating.
Report: severity-ranked issues, each with evidence and a recommended change.
